objective_compliance.description: Executable Object Code complies with HLR in normal range (§6.4.a)
objective_compliance.evidence: 24/24 assertions PASS across TC01~TC11; all SR-1(3 clauses+key observation), HLR-1(10 items), LLR-1(11 items) have corresponding test coverage; dual-compiler zero warnings; channel independence verified; per-cycle behavior confirmed.

objective_compliance.description: Executable Object Code is robust with HLR (§6.4.b)
objective_compliance.evidence: Core negative-side paths covered (valid+inconsistent→suppress: PASS; invalid→suppress: PASS; consecutive suppress: PASS; channel isolation: PASS). Gaps: LA/LB fourth sub-case(invalid+inconsistent, TC-16-001 not independently executed), extreme-value/micro-difference boundaries(TC-13/TC-14) not tested in DA-10, 4 TCs suspended due to unresolved AMBs. For DAL D core negative-sides are sufficient; gaps should be filled post-AMB resolution.

objective_compliance.description: Executable Object Code is compatible with target computer (§6.4.e)

All runtime target-env verifications deferred (41 hardware TTP): compare results alignment(Cortex-M4 vs host), fixed-cycle scheduling stability, EQC/EQB interface timing on target. LLR-AMB-08 unresolved further delays memcmp suitability confirmation (TC-19-002).

process_data.analysis_methodology: Cross-referenced DA-10 test execution results(11 TCs, 24 assertions) against full 44-TC case list and 33 requirement items(SR-1, HLR-1, LLR-1). Verified each requirement has at least one executing TC ID mapping.
